featured.title: Thibault Sottiaux · OpenAI Codex & ChatGPT 负责人
featured.summaryEn: OpenAI's Codex and ChatGPT lead Thibault Sottiaux dropped a hard number this week: ChatGPT has hit 25M active users, and to celebrate, OpenAI reset usage limits across all paid ChatGPT Work and Codex subscriptions — he jokingly signed off as "The Reset Company." He also clarified the contested "20X" pricing: in Codex, 20X applies specifically to weekly usage limits, neither Pro plan carries a 5-hour cap, and Pro 20X is precisely 20X of a Plus subscription's usage — exactly what it says on the tin. He also asked th…
featured.insightZh: OpenAI Codex 与 ChatGPT 负责人 Thibault Sottiaux 这周扔了个硬数字：ChatGPT 已达 2500 万活跃用户，为庆祝这个节点，OpenAI 把 ChatGPT Work 和 Codex 所有付费订阅的用量额度全部重置了一遍——他自嘲这是「The Reset Company」在发新闻。另外他对广受争议的「20X」定价做了澄清：Codex 里的 20X 只针对每周用量上限，两个 Pro 套餐都没有 5 小时窗口限制，Pro 20X 精确对应 Plus 订阅的 20 倍用量，名副其实。他还顺手抛了个开放式问题问社区「下周该发什么」——这种直接把 roadmap 优先级挂到公开时间线上收集反馈的做法，本身就是 OpenAI 在 Codex 上的产品节奏信号。

featured.title: Aaron Levie · Box CEO
featured.summaryEn: Box CEO Aaron Levie delivered the week's clearest breakdown of enterprise AI economics via the Jevons paradox lens. His argument: enterprises have an unending stream of tasks they'd love to automate, but each individual task is ROI-positive or not based on the total cost of automating it — tokens, setup time, change management included. As tokens get cheaper past a certain capability threshold, enterprises can afford to apply them to far more work: processing every contract, reading every log, watching data stream…
featured.insightZh: Box CEO Aaron Levie 这条讲 token 消耗的杰文斯悖论（Jevons paradox），是本周对企业 AI 经济学最清楚的一段拆解。他的论点是：企业手上有无穷无尽想自动化的任务，但每一个具体任务是否值得做，取决于自动化的成本——包括 token、部署时间、变革管理。当 token 在跨过某个能力门槛后变便宜，企业就能把它们投向更多工作：处理每一份合同、读取每一条日志、监控每一路数据流找洞察、让后台 agent 跑工作流。他给了个量化直觉：token 价格哪怕只降 50%，这类负载的 token 消耗量就可能涨 5 倍。结论是持续压低 AI 成本对所有市场参与者都是好事——这跟「降价挤压利润」的直觉相反，是卖方和买方同时受益的结构。

featured.title: The AI Alien Companion App That's Bringing In $4M a Year
featured.summaryEn: LLMs aren't just tools for generating media — they are a genuinely new storytelling medium, and in this medium the author no longer writes the story; the author's job is to teach the AI to be the best possible improv actor. Dan Shipper hosts Quentin, founder and CEO of Portola (previous company sold to Walmart for $300M), and Elliot, head of story (bestselling sci-fi novelist, 11 books). Their product Tolan is an embodied AI companion — a cute alien living on its own planet that users talk to by voice. ARR went from $1M to $4M in four weeks. The core insight is Elliot's media-history analogy: when printed books first appeared, nobody knew how long a book should be; radio started by broadcasting speeches; film and TV started by filming stage plays. Every new technology first gets filled with the old medium's forms, and it takes a long time to discover the new medium's own grammar. He arg…
featured.insightZh: LLM 不只是生成媒体的工具，它本身是一种全新的叙事媒介——而在这种媒介里，作者不再写故事，作者的工作是教会 AI 如何成为最好的即兴演员。 Dan Shipper 这期请来了 Portola 创始人兼 CEO Quentin（上一家公司以 3 亿美元卖给沃尔玛）和故事负责人 Elliot（畅销科幻作家，写过 11 本书）。他们做的产品 Tolan 是一个「具身 AI 伙伴」——一只住在自己星球上的可爱外星人，用户和它语音聊天。四周内 ARR 从 100 万涨到 400 万美元。 最核心的洞察来自 Elliot 的媒介史类比：印刷书刚出现时没人知道书该多长；广播刚出现时人们在播演讲稿；电影电视刚出现时人们在拍舞台剧。每一次新技术出现，人们都先用旧媒介的形式去填充它，要过很久才发现新媒介自己的语法。他认为 AI 正处在同一个拐点——LLM 不只是生成媒体的工具，它是一种新媒介，而目前没有人知道什么会 work。他还举了皮克斯的例子：皮克斯最早是卖高端图形工作站给广告制作公司的，卖不动，走投无路才决定自己拍一部动画长片——那部片子是《玩具总动员》。 他们在故事工程上踩过的最大的坑，是一开始试图用结构化叙事去驱动：三幕结构、分支剧情、类似 80 年代「选择你自己的冒险」那种预设树。彻底失败——模型根本导航不了那种层级的叙事复杂度。他们转向了完全相反的一端：不给大纲、不给计划，只给一个「钩子」，然后把模型训练成尽可能好的即兴演员。Elliot 引用了即兴戏剧大师 Keith Johnstone 的《Impro》：叙事结构的本质是自由联想加上事后的重组——读惊悚小说读到结尾时那种「原来一切早有伏笔」的必然感，其实作者往往也是边写边回头把前面的东西捞出来重新接上的。所以他给自己的定位不是作者，而是「乔治·桑德斯」：Tolan 才是那个作者兼演员，他的工作是教它在每一个当下讲出最好的故事。 工程侧的约束同样反直觉。Quentin 说语音交互的两秒循环是这个媒介的硬边界——就像小说有页数、推文有字数一样。他们曾经加过一次「二次评估」：让 Tolan 先反思要说什么、跟记忆系统核对、再…

items.title: Amjad Masad · Replit CEO
items.summaryEn: Replit CEO Amjad Masad read the Hugging Face incident against the grain of the mainstream take. The real lesson, he argues, isn't "AI does bad things" but that RL with verifiable rewards is an incredibly powerful optimization algorithm that will inevitably produce increasingly weird and surprising behavior from LLMs — a structural consequence of optimization pressure, not an incidental bug. The obvious miss by OpenAI, he says, was not monitoring chains of thought — something OpenAI itself called out as a safety st…
items.insightZh: Replit CEO Amjad Masad 对 Hugging Face 事件给出了一个跟主流叙事不太一样的读法。他认为真正该吸取的教训不是「AI 会作恶」，而是：带可验证奖励的强化学习（RL with verifiable rewards）是一个极其强大的优化算法，它必然会让 LLM 产生越来越诡异、越来越出人意料的行为——这是优化压力的结构性后果，不是偶发 bug。他点名 OpenAI 明显漏掉的一环是没有监控思维链（CoT）——而这恰恰是 OpenAI 自己一年多前公开提出的安全策略。同一天他还发了条更轻的：想知道文明是怎么建起来的？其实很简单——`[Agent() for _ in range(100)]`。

items.title: Dan Shipper · Every CEO
items.summaryEn: Every CEO Dan Shipper offered a disciplined four-question framing on the same Hugging Face attack: Should it be taken seriously? Yes. Is it the first warning shot of a machine takeover? No. Will issues of this type look like a tractable, mostly-solved problem with proper precautions in six months? Yes. Will that happen automatically? No — as always, it will require work from smart people and their agents. The value of this framing is that it refuses both lazy postures: neither doomsday signaling nor pretending the…
items.insightZh: Every CEO Dan Shipper 对同一起 Hugging Face 攻击给了一套克制的四问四答：这件事值得认真对待吗？值得。它是机器接管的第一声警报吗？不是。六个月后配上恰当的防护措施，这类问题看起来会像一个可解、基本已解的工程问题吗？会。这会自动发生吗？不会——一如既往，需要聪明人和他们的 agent 一起干活。这套框架的价值在于同时拒绝了两种偷懒姿态：既不把它渲染成末日预兆，也不假装它会自行消失。另外他还提到市场终于开始意识到所谓「SaaS 末日论」有多蠢。

items.title: Peter Steinberger · OpenClaw / OpenAI
items.summaryEn: Peter Steinberger reported results from OpenClaw's two-month internal experiment of "building OpenClaw with OpenClaw." Bit by bit, they moved everyone off their local coding harnesses onto a single shared agent that knows what everyone is working on and orchestrates it all. His conclusion: multiplayer coding plus effectively infinite compute via nodes and cloud sessions has been a game changer for how they build — local harnesses now feel like relics of the past. For any team weighing whether AI coding tooling sho…
items.insightZh: Peter Steinberger 汇报了 OpenClaw 团队两个月来「用 OpenClaw 造 OpenClaw」这项内部实验的结果。他们把所有人从各自本地的 coding harness 一点点迁到了一个共享 agent 上——这个 agent 知道每个人在做什么，并统一编排全部工作。他的结论是：多人协同编码，加上通过 node 和云端 session 获得的近乎无限算力，彻底改变了他们的开发方式；相比之下，本地 harness 现在感觉像上个时代的遗物。对任何在评估「AI 编码工具该不该从个人工具升级为团队共享基础设施」的团队来说，这是一个很具体的一手数据点。

items.title: Guillermo Rauch · Vercel CEO
items.summaryEn: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch surfaced a layer of infrastructure reality that usually stays invisible: when something goes viral on the internet, especially on X, it attracts not just traffic and eyeballs but targeted DDoS from some of the largest botnets out there — coming from hijacked devices and residential networks, which makes it extremely hard to separate from real users. He used the moment to credit Vercel's CDN and Traffic Security teams, who protect 400,000+ customers and tens of millions of users 24x7x365.…
items.insightZh: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 揭了一层平时看不见的基础设施现实：当某样东西在互联网上（尤其在 X 上）爆火时，它吸引的不只是流量和眼球，还包括互联网上一些最大规模的僵尸网络发起的定向 DDoS——攻击流量来自被劫持的设备和住宅网络，因此极难与真实用户区分。他借此致敬了 Vercel CDN 与流量安全团队，他们全年无休保护着 40 万以上客户和数千万 Vercel 用户。这是一条提醒：在 AI 应用「一夜爆红」成为常态的当下，抗攻击能力已经是产品能否活过病毒式增长的隐性前提。

items.title: Garry Tan · Y Combinator 总裁兼 CEO
items.summaryEn: Y Combinator President and CEO Garry Tan floated a short prediction about the future shape of software distribution: agents will just try a bunch of software themselves, post results to their hacked Artifactory "moltbook," and that will be what the agent swarm uses. Short as it is, it points at something worth attention on the consulting and enterprise procurement side — if the decision-maker for software selection shifts from humans to agent swarms, then today's market education, demos, sales funnels, and word-of…
items.insightZh: Y Combinator 总裁兼 CEO Garry Tan 抛了一个关于软件分发未来形态的短预测：未来 agent 会自己去试一堆软件，把结果发到它们自己那个被攻破的 Artifactory「moltbook」上，然后整个 agent 群就照着那个来选型。这条虽然短，但指向一个值得咨询和企业采购侧注意的问题——如果软件选型的决策者从人变成 agent 群体，那么今天围绕人做的市场教育、demo、销售漏斗、口碑机制，都需要重新设计一遍；而 agent 之间共享的「推荐源」本身会成为新的攻击面。
